nodes.content: Develop semantic parsers that generalize to unseen operator compositions despite training correlations between linguistic templates and program structure.
requirements: Achieve 80% exact-match accuracy on held-out operator compositions under reversed template–structure correlations.
Retain in-distribution exact-match accuracy within two percentage points of an identically sized, conventionally trained parser.

nodes.content: Train a size-matched parser with template-balanced utterance–program subtree recombinations and span-to-operator contrastive loss, retaining original examples.
Can template-balanced subtree swaps preserve quantifier and negation scope when their utterance spans overlap?
Scope-typed subtree swaps will maintain utterance–program scope agreement for at least 95% of overlapping negation–quantifier examples.
Annotate operator scopes, restrict swaps to compatible spans, and audit 200 overlapping negation–quantifier recombinations for scope agreement.
Annotate operator scopes, generate 200 compatible negation–quantifier swaps for ScopeSwap-200, and manually score utterance–program scope agreement.
On ScopeSwap-200, only 178/200 scope-typed swaps preserved utterance–program scope agreement (89%), below the 95% target.
Dominance-constrained scope swaps will achieve ≥95% scope agreement on 200 new overlapping negation–quantifier pairs, versus 89% without constraints.
Generate 200 new ScopeSwap pairs under dominance-constrained and unconstrained swaps; manually compare scope agreement against the 95% threshold.
On 200 paired ScopeSwap examples, dominance constraints yielded 194/200 scope-consistent swaps (97%), versus 179/200 (89.5%) unconstrained.
Use ScopeSwap-200's failure audit to select dominance-constrained swaps for augmentation; paired validation achieved 97% scope agreement.
Generate 10,000 dominance-constrained ScopeSwap pairs, then train the size-matched parser on augmented and original examples with span-to-operator contrastive loss.
ScopeSwap-10K v1 contains 10,000 dominance-constrained utterance–program pairs and checkpoints for the size-matched contrastive parser.
How can dominance-constrained swaps be incorporated alongside original examples and span-to-operator supervision without increasing parser size?
Train a size-matched operator-factorized decoder with template-adversarial representations and grammar-constrained composition, without synthetic examples.
Train the template-adversarial operator-factorized decoder; tune on development splits and compare reversed-composition and in-distribution exact match against a size-matched baseline.
Train an original-only, template-adversarial operator decoder; compare reversed-composition and in-distribution exact match with ScopeSwap-10K v1 checkpoints.
OperatorFactor v1 includes original-only decoder checkpoints, template-adversarial training configuration, and exact-match comparisons against ScopeSwap-10K v1.
Benchmark OperatorFactor v1 and ScopeSwap-10K v1 on reversed-template compositions and in-distribution splits, reporting exact match against a size-matched baseline.
On RevComp, held-out/in-distribution exact match was OperatorFactor 82%/91%, ScopeSwap-10K 74%/92%, and the conventional baseline 65%/92%.
Ablate template-adversarial loss and grammar constraints in OperatorFactor v1; measure RevComp exact match and template-probe accuracy.
Five-seed RevComp exact match averaged 77% for OperatorFactor (initial run: 82%), versus 83% without template-adversarial loss.
Prioritize grammar-constrained OperatorFactor without adversarial loss for in-distribution validation: five-seed RevComp exact match was 83% versus 77%.
Train a size-matched parser with operator-template group DRO and operator-preserving paraphrase consistency, retaining standard cross-entropy.
Will sparse operator-template groups cause group DRO to overfit rare templates and reduce in-distribution exact match?
Capping rare-group DRO weights at 3× will prevent overfitting, maintaining at least 90% five-seed in-distribution exact match.
Train five-seed group-DRO parsers with 3×-capped versus uncapped rare-group weights; compare in-distribution exact match and rare-template loss.
Across five seeds, capped group DRO reached 89% in-distribution exact match versus 86% uncapped, missing the 90% threshold.
Interpolating 3×-capped group DRO with cross-entropy at weight 0.3 will restore in-distribution exact match to ≥90% across five seeds.
Train five-seed parsers with 0.3-weight capped group DRO, cross-entropy, and operator-preserving paraphrase consistency; evaluate in-distribution and RevComp exact match.
Across five seeds, interpolated group DRO achieved 81% RevComp and 91% in-distribution exact match, versus 92% baseline in-distribution.
Use rule-based test-time template rewrites and type-checked AST consensus, retaining baseline predictions when consensus is weak.
Build scope-preserving rewrites, calibrate AST-consensus fallback on development data, then measure RevComp and in-distribution exact match against baseline.
Implement five scope-preserving template rewrites and type-checked AST voting; tune fallback margin on RevComp development data.
RewriteVote v1 packages five scope-preserving rewrite rules, type-checked AST voting, and development-calibrated baseline fallback.
Benchmark RewriteVote v1 on RevComp held-out compositions and in-distribution examples; report exact match against the conventional parser.
RewriteVote v1 achieved 73% RevComp exact match versus the 80% target; in-distribution accuracy was 92%, matching baseline.
Pretrain a size-matched parser on independently sampled ASTs with neutral grammar renderings, then fine-tune with original-data replay.
Can original-data replay close the neutral-rendering gap without reinstating template–structure shortcuts?
Mixing 25% original examples during fine-tuning will yield ≥80% RevComp and ≥90% in-distribution exact match across five seeds.
Pretrain on independently sampled AST renderings; fine-tune five seeds with 25% original-data replay and measure RevComp/in-distribution exact match.
Across five seeds, 25% original-data replay yielded 84% RevComp and 90% in-distribution exact match, meeting both thresholds.
Compare five-seed RevComp and in-distribution exact match for full OperatorFactor, its grammar-only ablation, interpolated group DRO, and 25%-replay pretraining.
Five-seed RevComp exact match: full OperatorFactor 77%, grammar-only 83%, group DRO 81%, replay pretraining 84%; DRO/replay maintained 91%/90% in-distribution.
Does replay pretraining outperform group DRO on three-operator RevComp cases while retaining at least 90% in-distribution exact match?
On three-operator RevComp cases, 25%-replay pretraining will exceed group DRO by ≥5 accuracy points while retaining ≥90% in-distribution exact match.
Stratify five-seed RevComp predictions by operator count; compare replay pretraining and group DRO exact match on three-operator cases.
On composition-balanced RevComp, group DRO scored 78% exact match versus replay’s 84%; three-operator scores were 73%/82%, with 91%/90% in-distribution.
Prioritize 25%-replay pretraining given its three-operator advantage; independently verify ≥80% RevComp and ≥90% in-distribution exact match.
Evaluate five fresh-seed 25%-replay parsers against size-matched baselines on sealed reversed-correlation RevComp and in-distribution splits; report exact-match means.
On sealed RevComp, five fresh-seed replay parsers averaged 83% held-out and 91% in-distribution exact match; baseline in-distribution was 92%.
Select 25%-replay pretraining over group DRO: sealed RevComp reached 83%/91% held-out/in-distribution exact match, with nine-point better three-operator accuracy.
Ablate ScopeSwap-10K v1 augmentation on the selected 25%-replay parser; measure held-out RevComp and in-distribution exact match.
Replay–ScopeSwap Ablation v1 contains paired checkpoints with and without ScopeSwap-10K augmentation and per-seed RevComp/in-distribution exact-match tables.
